records.statement: The RIL activation tests verify that role activation requires an available role authorized for the exact requested scope, that authorization scopes remain independent, and that activation itself creates no authority.
The activation tests verify fail-closed behavior for malformed evidence, unknown activation methods, unassigned scopes, unavailable authorized roles, and conflicting authorization projections.
The admission tests verify that admission requires independent admission authority and that a reconciliation recommendation alone is not admission authority.
The admission tests verify first admission requires explicit project identity and successful first admission writes schema-valid project-seeded PEMS/COVE plus immutable evidence.
The admission tests verify exact retry is no-change while candidate mutation after reconciliation, stale plans, record collisions, and conflicting second admission fail closed.
The authority-grant tests verify grant definitions are immutable, content-addressed, and idempotent and that non-delegable operations fail closed at grant creation.

The authority-grant tests verify an exact proposal must be wholly contained by grant scope and that partial/unknown effects, workflow mismatch, terminal workflow state, stale D3, and materiality pauses block issuance.
The authority-grant tests verify approval limits are consumed at issuance, revocation blocks future issuance without invalidating past approval, and issuance/revocation use exact-head concurrency.

The grant-operation tests verify bounded delegated role changes and non-root operator disable can issue/apply through grants, while protected-root disable and non-delegable operator operations cannot.
The grant-operation tests verify grant creation requires operation-specific grantor capability and apply-time logic validates immutable grant issuance evidence.

The shared-orchestration tests verify delegable operator and role proposals can auto-advance through a common path while stale D3, materiality pauses, ambiguous grants, and workflow scope failures stop before grant consumption.
The shared-orchestration tests verify non-delegable proposals and absence of applicable grants return an approval boundary rather than manufacturing authority.
The automation-boundary tests verify materiality cannot be bypassed by an in-scope grant and is revalidated before grant consumption.

The automation-boundary tests verify stale state, exhausted or revoked grants, unresolved activation/conditions, grant ambiguity, wildcard inference, scope expansion, and protected operations all stop automation fail closed.

The autonomous-workflow tests verify a prospectively authorized chain can complete without Human interruption only while its accepted scope remains valid, with materiality, scope expansion, and protected authority causing interruption before the next consequential mutation.

The Human-Agent tests verify context-bound affirmations fail closed, proposal presentation exposes the exact immutable reference, and direct approval performs D3 revalidation immediately before approval creation.
The Human-Agent tests verify cross-session resume reconstructs from durable references and protected ceremonies plus final control return remain explicit adapter boundaries.

The cross-adapter tests verify Human-Agent and CLI surfaces preserve identical proposal, approval, D3, workflow, grant, event, continuation, and delegable-apply artifacts/results when routing the same operations.
The mutation tests verify canonical JSON/digest determinism, proposal creation without filesystem mutation, approval binding to exact proposals, append/replay behavior, and idempotent retries.

The mutation tests verify consumed approvals cannot authorize later transitions, stale bases fail without mutation, missing projections are rebuildable, conflicting projections fail closed, and corrupted/non-contiguous event chains are detected.

The initial-operator tests verify an empty project requires an initial operator ceremony, planning is deterministic and mutation-free, exact confirmation is required, and application creates exactly one protected root.
The initial-operator tests verify second distinct roots and conflicting projections are rejected and that initial-operator setup creates no Steward or canonical state.
The operator-management tests verify ordinary authorized managers may add, disable, re-enable, and capability-update non-root operators but cannot change the protected root.
The operator-management tests verify root transfer requires current-root approval, exact confirmation, an active target with all core capabilities, and preserves exactly one root after success.

The role-registry tests verify default Steward role presence does not create authority, role planning is deterministic, scoped snapshots affect only roles within scope, and forbidden protocol/package roles or unknown rd capabilities are rejected.
The role-registry tests verify unauthorized operators and conflicting projections fail closed and role changes create no semantic authority or canonical state.
The Steward-authorization tests verify scopes begin unassigned, the default Steward is not automatic, authorization scopes are independent, and reassignment/revocation affect only the selected scope.

The Steward-authorization tests verify unknown/unavailable targets and unauthorized operators are rejected, approval is bound to the exact proposal, projection conflicts fail closed, and authorization creates no semantic or canonical state.

The reconciliation tests verify activation authority is required, candidates must come from submissions, successful reconciliation persists immutable disposition and activation evidence, and no admission/canonical state is created.
The reconciliation tests verify conflicting second dispositions fail closed and candidate byte mutation creates a new identity rather than rewriting an existing disposition.

The storage-verification tests verify valid admitted state is verified read-only and deterministic, while missing/incomplete canonical pairs, noncanonical PEMS bytes, schema-invalid PEMS, COVE mismatch, receipt mismatch, and symlink canonical files fail.

The ordinary-repair tests verify missing, stale, or malformed projections can be rebuilt deterministically from valid history without touching history and invalid history requires exceptional recovery.

The exceptional-recovery tests verify valid history cannot be recovered, recovery is protected-root and evidence-backed, changed damage after approval fails closed, and later damage mutation is detected by recovery records.

The workflow tests verify immutable definition identity binds intent/authentication, auto-advance requires explicit prospective confirmation, extension events do not advance the normative head, and competing normative transitions fail stale-head checks.

The workflow tests verify materiality pauses suspend continuation, acknowledgements bind exact pauses, completion is primitive-proved and terminal, cancellation is requester/root-only, and revisions create successors while sealing predecessors.

The status tests verify lifecycle blockers have precedence, missing projections are classified rebuildable without mutation, authorization scopes remain independent, evidence/candidate presence never asserts semantic validity, and status is strictly read-only.

The orchestrator tests verify read-only routing preserves primitive results, unknown actions call no primitive, arguments are forwarded exactly, plan/approve/apply remain separate routes, reconciliation authority evidence is forwarded unchanged, and admit does not implicitly run storage verification.
The CLI tests verify bounded presentation depth, exclusive presentation modes, project override behavior, direct approval routing, and shared workflow-continuation routing.

The final CLI topology tests verify inventories are type-specific, content-artifact inspection cannot invent deeper semantics, aggregate history refuses a fabricated global chronology, and universal apply routes role mutations through the grant-aware boundary.
